senses.gloss:
Haṭhayoga
(‘yoga [that teaches the] union of प्राण and अपान’)
------------------------------------------
Haṭhayoga is one of the major branches of the योग system that teaches the practical aspects of spiritual life. ‘Yoga’ means the union of the जीव (the individual सोउल्) with परमात्मन् (God). The word ‘haṭha’ is split into two syllables, ‘ha’ and ‘ṭha’, and, interpreted as the ‘sun’ and the ‘moon’ or the ‘prāṇa’ and the ‘apāna’, the two important aspects of the prāṇic energy working in a living being. According to this explanation, हठयोग is the science of प्राणायाम that includes other aspects of योग also like āsanas and mudrās. (See ĀSANAS and MUDRĀS.)
According to the tradition described in the scriptures dealing with हठयोग, आदिनाथ or God शिव is the first teacher who taught it to his divine spouse पार्वती.
Some of the distinguished teachers of this tradition are: मत्स्येन्द्रनाथ, Gorakṣanātha, Śābarānanda, Mīnanātha, Bileśaya, भैरव, Manthāna, Kākacaṇḍīśvara, Prabhudeva (Allama Prabhu?) and others.
Haṭhayoga and राजयोग are two sides of the same coin. Neither is possible without the help of the other. However, the writers on हठयोग agree that राजयोग which deals with the control of the मिन्द् ultimately leading to समाधि, is primary and that the former is only an aid to it.
To practise हठयोग, a suitable place is needed. It should be clean and secluded, with a level ground. The air must be pure.
Yoga is destroyed by certain habits which, therefore, must be avoided. They are: atyāhāra (overeating), prayāsa (over-exertion), prajalpa (talkativeness), niyamā-graha (observance of unsuitable disciplines like ड़स्तिन्ग् etc.), janasaṅga (company of persons not spiritually inclined) and laulya (unsteadiness).
On the other hand, there are certain qualities which are conducive to योग and hence, need to be cultivated. They are: sāhasa (daring), utsāha (enthusiasm), dhairya (courage), tattvajñāna (true know-ledge), niścaya (firmness of faith in the words of the गुरु) and janasaṅgaparityāga (abandonment of unsuitable company).
Success in this योग is indicated by certain signs such as the body losing flabbiness and becoming lean, brightness of face and eyes, hearing of the anāhata-ध्वनि (sound of ओङ्कार), better health and appetite, purification of the nāḍīs and so on.
The steps of हठयोग as described in the standard works are generally four. They are: आसन (various postures like svastikāsana, gomukhāsana, वीरासन etc.); प्राणायाम (varieties of breath-control like sūryabheda, sītkārī and bhastrikā); मुद्रा (exercises for rousing the कुण्डलिनी such as mahāmudrā, khecarī, uḍḍiyāna and so on); nādānu-sandhāna (meditating on the inner sound produced by the rousing of the कुण्डलिनी).
See also RĀJAYOGA.

Haṭhayoga-pradīpikā
(‘a light [that reveals] हठयोग’)
------------------------------------------
The Haṭhayoga-pradīpikā of Svātmā-राम (A. D. 1350) along with the Gheraṇḍa Saṁhitā of Gheraṇḍa is a standard treatise dealing with the science of हठयोग. It has a commentary Jyotsnā, by one Brahmānanda.
It is in four chapters (called ‘Upa-deśa’) and has 389 verses in all. Though most of the verses are in the usual śloka metre, some are in longer metres also like the Vasantatilakā and Śārdūlavikrīḍitā.
The first chapter (67 verses) gives in the beginning a long list of the ancient teachers of this योग. This is followed by some details regarding its practice like the place suitable for it, evils to be avoided, virtues to be cultivated, some āsanas and details of diets suitable and unsuitable.
The second chapter (78 verses) deals with प्राणायाम (control of the prāṇic energy through the control of breath) and the षट्कर्मस् or the six acts of cleansing the internal parts of the body as also increasing its capacity for the sādhanās of हठयोग.
The third chapter, the biggest (130 verses) expounds in detail, the ten mudrās (exercises needed to rouse the कुण्डलिनी power).
The fourth, the last (114 verses), delineates समाधि which comes as a result of the rousing of the कुण्डलिनी. In समाधि, the मिन्द् will have dissolved in the आत्मन् even as salt in water. This section also gives a description of the योगि who has attained समाधि.
Experts warn the readers of such works not to attempt the various techniques of योग given in such works, without the direct guidance of proper teachers.
See also HAṬHAYOGA.
